identity.title: Learning Smooth and Expressive Interatomic Potentials for Physical Property Prediction

problem.claim: Determine whether MLIP test performance predicts downstream physical-property prediction performance.

gap.claim: Lower held-out test errors do not consistently yield better downstream physical-property predictions.

contributions.claim: Proposes testing MLIPs by their practical ability to conserve energy during molecular-dynamics simulations.
Identifies model choices associated with failing the energy-conservation test and uses these observations to improve expressive models.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper distinguishes MLIP quality through a molecular-dynamics energy-conservation test and uses its failure patterns to improve expressive models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, when the proposed test is passed, correlations improve between test errors and downstream physical-property performance.
The authors report that eSEN achieves state-of-the-art results across materials stability, thermal conductivity, and phonon prediction tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: MLIPs approximate quantum-mechanical calculations at lower computational cost.
Held-out test errors do not always predict downstream physical-property results.
The paper proposes evaluating practical energy conservation during molecular-dynamics simulations.
It examines choices linked to test failure and uses them to improve expressive models.
The resulting eSEN model is reported to perform strongly across several physical-property tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a domain-relevant behavioral test—energy conservation in molecular dynamics—to stronger correlations between test errors and downstream performance.

lessons.interpretation: A task-aligned diagnostic may make benchmark metrics more informative for deployment outcomes.
lessons.application: When introducing a predictive model, add a domain-behavior test and report whether passing it changes the relationship between benchmark error and target-task performance.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when the deployment domain lacks a meaningful behavioral or mechanistic diagnostic.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the pass criteria or implementation of the energy-conservation test.
It gives no quantitative correlations, benchmark scores, datasets, baselines, or details of the model choices linked to failure.
The basis and scope of the state-of-the-art comparison are unspecified.
